definition: Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KANs) are a type of artificial neural network architecture inspired by the Kolmogorov–Arnold representation theorem, also known as the superposition theorem.
details: Unlike traditional multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), which rely on fixed activation functions and linear weights, KANs replace each weight with a learnable univariate function, often represented using splines.
story: Imagine a factory floor where each workstation can glance at every other workstation before doing its part. Think of it this way: Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KANs) are a type of artificial neural network architecture inspired by the Kolmogorov–Arnold representation theorem, also known as the superposition theorem. And here is the clever part: Unlike traditional multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), which rely on fixed activation functions and linear weights, KANs replace each weight with a learnable univariate function, often represented using splines. Structure decides what the model can even express — the blueprint before the bricks. And that shape of the machine — Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks — is what makes everything else possible.
